w10_P4_003338: On a laboratory test track, a sled with a mass of 39000 g is held at rest until t = 1 s and then released, and from t = 1 s to t = 2 s its acceleration in m/s² follows 3t² + 8t, with t in seconds. The sled itself is 1.2 m long. At the instant t = 2 s a booster fires and multiplies the sled's speed by exactly 2. The engineer wants the energy the sled carries purely because of its motion right after the booster, but reduced by the 29 J that the rails have already turned into heat. What is that remaining energy, in kJ?
w10_P4_003344: A shipyard engineer needs the total force, in N, that 3 identical winch assemblies must supply together, where each winch drives 9 identical cables and each cable hauls 10 identical crates. Work back from the single crate: every crate has a mass of 148 kg, and the system must give each crate an acceleration, in m/s², equal to the largest whole number that divides both 170 and 229 with no remainder. The force on one crate is whatever is needed to produce that acceleration. A cable's pull is the combined force on its 10 crates, a winch's output is the combined pull of its 9 cables, and the 3 winches together give the figure required. What is that total force, in N?
w10_P4_003348: The number a drone team must report is a total energy budget in kJ, built as follows: the energy of motion of 8 identical drones, plus 22 kJ held in a spare battery pack, plus a further 26 kJ stored in the ground station's capacitor bank. Each drone has a mass of 14000 g and cruises at a speed, in m/s, equal to the number of different ways of choosing 2 waypoints out of 7. The hangar is kept at 18 °C throughout the test. Work out one drone's energy of motion and convert it to kJ before combining the 8 drones and then adding the two reserves in turn. What is the total budget, in kJ?
w10_P4_003349: A range officer wants the combined thrust, in N, of 2 identical booster stacks, each built from 12 identical motors, so first find one motor's net thrust. A test mass of 116 kg is mounted on a motor; from t = 2 s to t = 3 s the motor's acceleration grows at a rate of 5t² + 3t (in m/s³, with t in seconds), starting from zero acceleration at t = 2 s. The motor's raw thrust is the force needed to give the 116 kg mass the acceleration reached at t = 3 s. From that raw thrust subtract 20 N of aerodynamic drag, and then subtract a further 23 N of rail friction, to obtain one motor's net thrust. The test rail is 640 m long. What is the combined thrust of the 2 stacks, in N?
w10_P4_003352: An automated warehouse runs 6 identical shuttle carts in each aisle, and the building has 4 such aisles. Each cart has a mass of 48000 g and cruises at a speed, in m/s, equal to 2 times the sum of 2 and 16. A cart's energy budget is its energy of motion plus the 1 J held in its small onboard flywheel. An aisle's budget is the 6 cart budgets added together, less the 11 J that the aisle's shared brake resistor dissipates. Each aisle rail is 85 m long. What is the energy budget summed over all 4 aisles, in J?
w10_P4_003353: A maintenance trolley of mass 55000 g is pushed along a level factory floor with an acceleration a, in m/s², that satisfies a² − 5a + 4 = 0; the larger of the two possible values is the one actually achieved. The push on one such trolley is exactly the force needed to give it that acceleration. A train of 11 identical trolleys is coupled together and each receives the same push, so the total applied force is 11 times the single-trolley push. Of that total, 29 N is absorbed by the couplings and then a further 4 N by a dragging brake shoe. Express the force that remains, in kN.
w10_P4_003357: A crane operator tests a load whose mass is 179000 g. The load's acceleration, in m/s², is set by a dial code built in stages: start with the largest whole number that divides both 54 and 149 exactly, multiply it by 4, multiply the result by 7, and finally add 29. The hoist cable is 40 m long. The extra cable tension is the force needed to give the 179000 g load that acceleration. The crane performs 10 identical lifts in a shift, and the operator adds up that force over all 10 lifts. What is the summed force, in N?
w10_P4_003366: The figure the technician needs is a net energy in J, found from the following account. The energy of motion of 12 identical pucks is totalled, 21 J of that total is lost to friction on the air table, and then 15 J is added by a final tap of the launcher. Each puck has a mass of 44 kg and slides at a speed, in m/s, equal to the largest whole number that divides both 383 and 310 with no remainder. Compute one puck's energy of motion first and scale up to the 12 pucks before applying the loss and the addition. What is the net energy, in J?
w10_P4_003367: A cargo train on a mine railway is loaded with pallets, each of mass 86000 g, and the locomotive must give every pallet an acceleration, in m/s², equal to the sum of the terms 2k − 1 for k running from 1 to 5. The force on one pallet is the force required to produce that acceleration. A single wagon carries 8 such pallets, and the coupling on each wagon adds 5 N of its own to the wagon's force. Convert one wagon's force to kN. The train consists of 8 identical wagons. What is the total force over the whole train, in kN?
w10_P4_003370: The result required is a net energy in J: the energy of motion of a test vehicle at t = 2 s, minus 8 J lost in the tyres, minus 29 J lost to air resistance, minus a further 8 J of bearing loss, plus 28 J recovered by a regenerative brake. The vehicle has a mass of 28000 g and its position along a straight track is 3t³ + 3t² metres, with t in seconds. Use the vehicle's speed at t = 2 s to find its energy of motion. What is the net energy, in J?
w10_P4_003379: A quality inspector's final report figure is an energy in kJ: the output of a whole press line plus 3 kJ of standby energy. The press line has 9 identical presses, and each press holds 3 identical hammers. Each hammer has a mass of 8 kg and strikes at a speed, in m/s, equal to the sum of the terms 2k − 1 for k running from 1 to 6. A press's output is the energy of motion of its 3 hammers combined, and the line's output is the 9 presses combined, converted to kJ. What is the report figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_003381: The plant manager wants the total energy of motion, in kJ, of an entire fleet: 5 identical trucks, each towing 3 identical loaded pallet-trailers. Each trailer has a mass of 44 kg on the test scale and moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to 6 times the sum of 5 and 4. Work out one trailer's energy of motion and express it in kJ, combine the 3 trailers of one truck, and then combine the 5 trucks. What is the fleet total, in kJ?
w10_P4_003383: The quantity to find is a final energy reading in kJ, obtained by taking one probe's energy of motion in kJ, subtracting 2 kJ of instrument overhead, and multiplying by 4 because 4 identical probes are launched. Each probe has a mass of 51000 g. From t = 1 s to t = 2 s a probe's acceleration, in m/s², follows 2t² + 8t with t in seconds, and the probe is at rest at t = 1 s. The probe's energy of motion is taken at its speed at t = 2 s. What is the final reading, in kJ?
w10_P4_003384: A stamping machine's ram has a mass of 163 kg and is driven with an acceleration, in m/s², equal to 4 times the sum of 4 and 2. The machine's hydraulic supply runs at 210 bar. The drive force is what is needed to give the ram that acceleration; 26 N of it is absorbed by guide friction and then a further 22 N by seal drag, leaving the useful force. The shop floor has 3 identical machines, and their useful forces are added together, after which a 14 N offset on the load cell is added. What is the load cell's final reading, in N?
w10_P4_003394: The value a test engineer wants is a total pull in kN over 2 identical trains, each made up of 3 identical trucks. The pull on one truck is the force needed to give a 59000 g truck an acceleration, in m/s², equal to the sum of k for k running from 1 to 10, and this single-truck pull is expressed in kN. A train's pull is that of its 3 trucks combined. What is the total pull over the 2 trains, in kN?
w10_P4_003402: The number needed is the total energy of motion, in J, across an entire delivery: 5 identical vans, each carrying 7 identical racks, each rack holding 9 identical parcels. Every parcel has a mass of 52000 g, and on the conveyor each parcel moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to the largest whole number that divides both 355 and 183 with no remainder. Find the energy of motion of one parcel, then of one rack, then of one van, and then of the whole delivery. What is that total, in J?
w10_P4_003406: The figure to report is a final force in N: a single tug's net force multiplied by 4, because 4 identical tugs work the harbour. A tug tows a barge of mass 161000 g. The barge's acceleration, in m/s², is 5 times a base value x, where x is the smaller of the two numbers satisfying x² − 11x + 30 = 0. The tug's gross force is what is needed to give the barge that acceleration, and 20 N of it is lost to tow-line drag, leaving the net force. The tide is running at 3 km/h. What is the final force, in N?
w10_P4_003412: A bottling plant's conveyor pushes crates, each of mass 16 kg, with an acceleration, in m/s², equal to the number of ways of choosing 2 bottles from a row of 10. The force on one crate is what is required to produce that acceleration. A line carries 11 crates at once, so the line's force is 11 times the single-crate force; express it in kN. The motor controller then adds a bias of 15 kN to the line's force. The plant runs 5 identical lines, and the supervisor totals the biased line forces. What is that total, in kN?
w10_P4_003422: The answer sought is a remaining force in N, found by taking the total force on a rack of 7 identical robots, subtracting 29 N of cable drag and then subtracting a further 19 N of bearing friction. Each robot has a mass of 197000 g and is accelerated at a, in m/s², where a is the smaller of the two values satisfying a² − 6a + 5 = 0. The force on one robot is the force required to give it that acceleration. The rack sits in a room held at 21 °C. What is the remaining force, in N?
w10_P4_003435: A rocket-sled test uses a probe of mass 23000 g whose velocity along the rail is 3t³ + 5t² m/s, with t in seconds. From the probe's acceleration at t = 2 s, subtract 24 m/s² that the rail's incline accounts for and then a further 4 m/s² lost to drag, giving the net acceleration the thrusters supply. The force from one thruster is what is needed to give the probe that net acceleration. A sled carries 12 identical thrusters, and the test programme uses 10 identical sleds. What is the total thruster force over the programme, in N?
w10_P4_003439: The quantity to report is a net signed force in kN, with forward taken as positive: one cart's forward driving force in kN, minus 16 kN of opposing retarder force, multiplied by 5 because 5 identical carts share the retarder, plus 3 kN of forward assist from a booster. Each cart has a mass of 63000 g and is driven with an acceleration a, in m/s², where a is the larger of the two values satisfying a² − 9a + 20 = 0. The driving force on a cart is whatever is required to give it that acceleration. What is the net signed force, in kN?
w10_P4_003441: The number required is a total energy in J for 11 identical test batches, each batch made of 12 identical projectiles. A projectile has a mass of 43 kg, and the launch barrel is 2.4 m long. The launcher's speed setting, in m/s, is numerically equal to the rate at which the slope of the curve y = 4x³ + 5x² is itself changing at x = 2, with 6 added to it. Find one projectile's energy of motion at that speed, combine the 12 projectiles of a batch, and then combine the 11 batches. What is the total, in J?
w10_P4_003450: A workbench cart with a mass of 31000 g is released from rest at t = 0 s, and from t = 0 s to t = 1 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 1t² + 0t with t in seconds. Its speed at t = 1 s gives its energy of motion. 3 identical carts are released this way, and their energies of motion are added together. To that sum the technician adds 27 J supplied by a spring latch and then subtracts 7 J absorbed by a damper. What is the resulting energy, in kJ?
w10_P4_003453: The value to report is a net energy balance in kJ, with energy gained counted positive and energy spent counted negative: one cart's energy of motion in kJ, minus 30 kJ spent by the launcher's compressor, multiplied by 3 because 3 identical carts are launched, plus 11 kJ recovered by a regenerative brake. Each cart has a mass of 12000 g. The cart starts from rest at t = 2 s, and from t = 2 s to t = 3 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 1t² + 6t, with t in seconds; its energy of motion is taken at its speed at t = 3 s. The launch track is 15 m long. What is the net energy balance, in kJ?
w10_P4_003457: In a foundry, a ladle carriage of mass 118 kg runs on rails from a hydraulic supply at 160 bar. Its acceleration, in m/s², is 9 times the largest whole number that divides both 164 and 335 with no remainder. The drive force is what is required to give the carriage that acceleration. Of that force, 26 N is taken up by rail friction, and afterwards an 18 N push from a helper spring is added. What is the resulting force, in N?
